provenance.notes: Int family batch. Licensed, big-ticket, northern-state specialty; copy leans on moisture first, egress and code, and layouts. No waterproofing, egress or financing brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Dampness and efflorescence checks, sump pumps, interior drain tile, foundation crack sealing, vapour barriers, insulated wall systems, and why nobody should frame over a wet wall
pageStructurePlus.why: Every basement buyer has heard about mould behind new drywall. Showing the dry-first process is what makes a careful finisher worth the bigger number.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Egress window sizes and window wells, ceiling height rules, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, what makes a legal bedroom versus a bonus room, and who pulls the permit
pageStructurePlus.why: A basement bedroom adds value only if it's legal. Buyers planning for teens, in-laws or resale decide once they understand egress.

pageStructurePlus.section: Basement layout ideas with floor plans
pageStructurePlus.contains: Family rooms, home theatres, wet bars, home gyms, guest suites with a bath, home offices and playrooms, each with a sample floor plan around the stairs and mechanicals
pageStructurePlus.why: Basement buyers start with how they'll use the space, not with materials. Seeing a layout that fits their foundation turns a dream into a quote request.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Ejector pits and up-flush toilets, breaking and patching the slab, venting, adding a shower or a laundry, and how a bathroom changes the timeline and permit
pageStructurePlus.why: The bathroom is the biggest single cost swing in a basement. Explaining it early sets a realistic budget band.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Soffits around ducts and beams, drywall versus drop ceilings, keeping access to the furnace, water heater and shutoffs, and sound insulation under kitchens and bedrooms
pageStructurePlus.why: Low ceilings and boxed ducts are what make a finished basement feel like a basement. Showing solutions wins the buyer who wants it to feel like the main floor.

openers.line: A family in {City} pricing a basement finish finds your listing, sees the stars, and has no website to tap. They never see a single finished basement of yours.

openers.linkLine: Here's what a basement buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing links to Facebook. Someone planning a basement with a bedroom and bath wants floor plans and a budget band, not a scroll through job-site posts.

openers.linkLine: Your basements organised for the buyer, not the feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The basement site on your listing has a free-host banner and a gallery from a few years back. People about to spend this much on a lower level notice the date.

openers.linkLine: Your basement company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site's basement gallery won't scroll on my phone. People shopping for a basement finish are usually standing at the bottom of the stairs looking at bare concrete.

openers.line: Everyone thinking about finishing a basement searches what it costs before calling. Nobody in {City} answers that clearly, which is the opening for you.

openers.linkLine: A basement budget-band page, in your words: {demo-link}

openers.line: That basement bar with the stone wall and the theatre with the stepped seating are strong basement finishing work. Sorted by room type, they'd sell the next one.

openers.linkLine: Your basements sorted by bar, theatre, suite and family room: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a basement that's stayed dry through every spring melt and an inspector who passed it first time. That's the worry buyers have, and it's hidden on Maps.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about dryness, inspections or timeline. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the basements they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Basement finishing is winter work, and families start planning it when the kids are stuck indoors in October. The finisher they find then gets the winter schedule.
openers.hook: Use this September to November. Mention winter in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A basement site ready for the winter project season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Couples measure the basement on a Sunday and agree on a family room and bath. If there's no form, they wait for Monday and call whoever answers first.
openers.hook: Call their listed number on a weekend. If voicemail only and no form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A basement consultation request that works on weekends: {demo-link}

openers.line: That help-wanted post for a basement framer will get more serious replies if applicants can see the finished lower levels they'd be building.

openers.linkLine: A basement site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You finish basements around {City}, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you work there, and the permit office is different in every town.

openers.linkLine: A basement page for each town, with its permit notes: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment options on basement finishing, it should be on the budget page. A full lower level is the kind of project people need to see split up first.

openers.linkLine: Basement payment options explained before the consultation: {demo-link}

openers.line: A basement adds bedrooms, wiring and plumbing below grade. A page showing your licence, insurance and how inspections work answers the biggest worry before the first visit.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry. Note that a record exists; never quote a number.
openers.linkLine: Licence, permits and inspections on one basement page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your basements come from builders and past clients. That works until new-home starts slow, and even referrals search basement finishers by name.
openers.hook: Look for posts or reviews naming a builder or a neighbour. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a basement referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted doesn't look like a basement at all, which is the whole point. It should be the first thing a buyer sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest finished basement and name it by room type and finish.

objections.objection: I get my basements from builders and referrals.
objections.handler: "Then your basements sell themselves. Builders slow down, though, and a referred couple still searches you before letting a crew into the house for two months. The site is where they land."

objections.objection: Every basement is different, I can't publish prices.
objections.handler: "Agreed, so we publish bands by scope: open family room, with a bath, with a bedroom and egress. Your words, your bands. It filters out people expecting a weekend job."

objections.objection: Summer is slow and I'm not spending now.
objections.handler: "Summer is exactly when to build it. Basement planning starts in early autumn, and the site needs to be found before then."

objections.objection: I pay for remodeling leads already.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several finishers at once and you pay either way. Your own site sends that family to one basement company, you."

objections.objection: My office manager runs our Facebook.
objections.handler: "Keep it going. The site is for strangers comparing basement bids, and every Facebook post can point back to it."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: layouts by room, a moisture page, a budget band and a consultation form. Well under what one egress window costs."

bullets: Peg the build to a sliver of one finished basement, never to an hourly rate. Finishers think in projects and draws.
The budget-band page is the core. Bands by scope (open room, plus bath, plus bedroom) belong inside the build.
Layout pages (theatre, bar, suite, gym) are separate lines; each answers its own search and its own buyer.
Only quote a waterproofing section for finishers who do or manage moisture work themselves.
Town pages matter more here than in most trades because permits and egress rules vary by town.
Launch by late summer. Basement planning season runs autumn into winter.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a sample floor plan, a budget band and its own gallery of finished basements of that type.

lineItems.item: Consultation form with size, use and bath fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload of the bare basement, a moisture question, ceiling height, bath and bedroom checkboxes and routing.
Max with step photos from their own jobs, a dampness self-check and sump pump notes.
Max when it covers several towns' egress and permit notes and a legal-bedroom checklist.
Max when the story has the floor plan, the budget band, the timeline and a client quote.
Max when each page has local permit notes and finished basements from that town.

whatElseYouSell.name: Basement photo day with wide-angle and twilight shots
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Basements are hard to shoot: low light, low ceilings. A proper wide-angle day across three finished basements makes them look like the main floor."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a finished theatre or bar.

whatElseYouSell.name: Floor plan renderings for consultations
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Couples can't picture bare concrete as a family room. A rendered basement floor plan at the second meeting helps them sign."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, for their next big consultation.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile updates for finished basements
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your Maps listing gets a new lower-level reveal each week, a bar in one town, a guest suite in the next, so searchers see basements, not a blank profile."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at basement sign-off
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "On final inspection day the family gets a text asking for a review, while they're standing in the new basement."

whatElseYouSell.name: Autumn basement planning campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A September push for 'finish the basement this winter' catches families as the kids go back inside."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in September.

whatElseYouSell.name: Long-cycle basement follow-up emails
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Basement decisions take months. A monthly note with a finished lower level and a budget tip keeps you the finisher they remember."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the form has a list of people deciding.

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite yard sign and dumpster banner
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A basement job means a dumpster in the driveway for weeks. A banner and yard sign turn neighbours' curiosity into calls."

withoutAI.whoPays: The waterproofing company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Plenty of basement calls start with a damp wall you send to a waterproofer. That waterproofer needs a site too, and the two of you trade customers all year."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Waterproofers and finishers hand customers to each other constantly; one introduction is warm.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The crew that cuts your egress windows needs a site that explains sizes and wells, and your bedroom basements are the proof."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A specialist with steady demand and usually no site.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every basement theatre you build needs screens and speakers wired in. The AV company needs a site that shows those rooms."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: AV installers sell high tickets and share the best basement photos.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Builders sell homes with bare basements. A post-closing finish page routes those buyers to one basement company."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders like happy buyers and a vendor who shows up organised.

withoutAI.whoPays: The radon contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Radon testing often happens before a basement gets finished. The radon company needs a site, and their customers need a finisher."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same basement, consecutive steps, natural two-way referral.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "People buying a rack and a treadmill need somewhere to put them. A dealer page with basement gym builds sends them to you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers sell more when the room exists, and the finisher gets the gym builds.

withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners upload photos of stains and cracks and get a plain first read on what an inspector should check."
withAI.whyItWorks: Waterproofers burn drives on non-issues. A pre-screen books the real ones.

withAI.route: Egress size checker for egress installers
withAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners enter their window and well measurements and see whether it could qualify for a bedroom, then book a site visit."
withAI.whyItWorks: Egress questions are repetitive and the answer drives the sale.

withAI.pitchLine: "Customers enter the basement room size and get a draft screen, seating and speaker layout to bring to the consultation."
withAI.whyItWorks: It turns browsers into booked design visits.

withAI.route: Builder buyer-question bot on basement options
withAI.pitchLine: "New-home buyers ask about finishing the basement later. A bot answers from the builder's plans and routes them to one basement finisher."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders cut sales-office time, and the finisher gets warm leads.

withAI.pitchLine: "After a basement is finished, the radon contractor's past customers get a retest reminder, and the follow-up writes itself."
withAI.whyItWorks: Retests are recurring revenue the radon company forgets to chase.

withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers enter their basement ceiling height and floor area and see which racks and machines fit, with a finisher to call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Ceiling height kills home gym sales. Answering it up front saves returns.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for basement consultations
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Framing downstairs with no signal? Callers get a text asking the basement's size, whether it's ever been wet, and what they want down there."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Basement budget-band calculator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the basement square footage, pick open room, bath, bedroom or bar, and see the band before booking a consultation."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real bands by scope and size, and the minimum project.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that name the lower level
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a family reviews their new basement theatre or guest suite, a thank-you that mentions it is waiting for your okay."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Draw schedule billing for basement stages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit, then draws at framing inspection, drywall and final, sent automatically when you mark each basement stage done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their draw schedule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Bare-basement photo to layout sketch
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The family uploads photos of the bare basement and the stairs, and it drafts a layout around the mechanicals to react to before the visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their common layouts and past floor plans to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Basement project board from design to final inspection
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every basement on one board: design, permit, framing inspection, rough-ins, insulation, drywall, final, with the sub for each stage."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the form is producing. Needs their stages, inspections and subs.

softwareAI.name: Evening basement consultation line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, asks about size, moisture, bath and bedroom plans, and books the in-home basement consultation."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar, scopes and screening questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Moisture and pre-framing checklist log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before any basement framing, the crew logs moisture readings, crack repairs and vapour barrier photos. If a wall is ever questioned, the record exists."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their pre-framing checklist and a foreman to test it.

softwareAI.name: Family portal with basement progress and selections
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The family sees this week's basement progress, the next inspection date and the carpet and lighting picks they still owe."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the project board first.

softwareAI.name: Basement takeoff for framing and drywall
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Draw the basement walls and soffits and it drafts studs, insulation, drywall sheets and trim for the lumber order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their framing rules and past material lists. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Permit and inspection date reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each basement's permit filing, framing, insulation and final inspections get a reminder so drywall never goes up early."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs which towns require which inspections.

softwareAI.name: Change order notes from the basement walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Find a crack weeping behind the old paneling, say it into the phone, and it drafts the change order with cost and days for the family to sign."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their change order template and rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sub schedule for electricians, plumbers and drywallers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each sub sees which basement they're in next and gets a text when an inspection moves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run several basements at once. Needs sub list and typical sequence.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on egress, moisture and basement budgets
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can I put a bedroom in my basement' and 'what if it got wet once' at midnight, from your own basement rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ, bands and lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sump and dehumidifier check-in reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each spring, past basement clients get a reminder to test the sump and empty the dehumidifier, with a link to book a check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with dates and a check-visit price.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by basement scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether open family rooms, suites with baths or bar builds actually pay once subs, materials and change orders are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs invoices and hours for a season of basements.

softwareAI.name: Layout and town page writer for basements
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Monthly drafts of pages like 'basement guest suite with egress', built from your project notes and approved before they go live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs project notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Design agreement builder for basement plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Turn a basement consultation into a paid design agreement, with the floor plan fee credited to the build."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for finishers who charge for design. Needs their design fee and a past agreement.

softwareAI.name: Lumber and drywall price tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When stud and drywall prices move at the yard, the basement calculator and open quotes update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the calculator. Needs the yard's price sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Framer and finisher applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Basement framer and finish carpenter applicants answer your usual questions, and you only call the ones with real experience below grade."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the basement calculator for finishers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Basement finishers across the snow belt answer the same cost question. The budget-band calculator I built answers it for all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first basement client taught you the workflow and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer locator for a basement wall-panel or waterproofing system maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A maker of basement wall panels sells through dealers nobody can find online. A dealer map with warranty sign-up fixes that, and I know the basement side."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer marketing and need trade-fluent builders.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a basement page set with a moisture page, an egress page and a budget band as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need benefits members use. One deal reaches many.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with basement clients start from zero. License my template with layouts, egress and moisture pages built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished basement module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Basement franchisees each need town permit pages and a consultation form routed by ZIP code. One template, filled per territory."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Post-closing basement program for production builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every buyer of a home with an unfinished basement gets a link to finish it later, with plans drawn for that model."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders earn goodwill and referral fees; the finisher gets every model's layout pre-drawn.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Families turning basements into in-law suites need a guide to egress, kitchens and permits, with vetted finishers attached."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Housing programs need contractors who know the code, and basement suites are a growing ask.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Waterproofing and finishing joint lead network
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Waterproofers hand dry basements to finishers and the reverse. A shared referral board makes the swap formal across a metro."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Both trades want the other's customers; a small fee per company covers it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Basement project cost sheet for renovation lenders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A quarterly summary of local basement scopes, built only from bids finishers choose to share, helps lenders sanity-check loans."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Built from contributed bids, it never claims more than the bids show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home inspector basement findings referral portal
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Inspectors flag damp basements and unpermitted rooms. A portal sends those buyers to waterproofers and basement finishers after closing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Inspectors look good offering next steps, and both trades get warm buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Basement finisher in the next snow-belt metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A basement client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one basement company per metro. {City} has one. The next cold-weather metro with bare basements doesn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The basement finisher with a half-built site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Basement sites left half-done with no layouts or budget band are common. I finish them on a template that's already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already chose to buy once.

upsellLadder.line: "Three basements at different inspections is too much for a notebook. Let's put them on one board."

upsellLadder.line: "Last year's basements need a spring sump check. Each visit is a chance at the next room."
